analysis.investment_thesis: PNGJL trades at an earnings yield of only ~3.4% (EBIT ₹337 Cr / EV ~₹9,897 Cr), far below the Magic Formula's 12%+ threshold, making it significantly overvalued by this framework despite decent ROCE of 19.4%. The capital-intensive, inventory-heavy jewelry model requires constant working capital funding that obliterates free cash flow, disqualifying it as a "good and cheap" business.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 25.3% over 5 years (₹2,458 Cr → ₹7,586 Cr) demonstrates strong execution
ROCE of 19.4% and ROE of 21% are decent but not exceptional for the Magic Formula
Net profit CAGR of 51.9% shows operating leverage as scale builds
key_risks: Earnings yield of ~3.4% (EBIT/EV) — needs to be 12%+ for Magic Formula attractiveness; stock is ~3.5x overvalued on this metric
FCF crashed to -₹1,109 Cr in FY25 as working capital consumed IPO proceeds; jewelry retail structurally destroys FCF during growth phases
Borrowings nearly tripled in one year (₹455 Cr → ₹1,291 Cr) to finance gold inventory — creates significant commodity and credit risk
red_flags: OCF turned sharply negative at -₹675 Cr in FY25 after being positive in 4 of prior 5 years — growth is not self-funding
Operating margin of only 6.94% on ₹7,586 Cr revenue means thin cushion against gold price swings or demand slowdown
Post-IPO asset base ballooned from ₹1,465 Cr to ₹4,341 Cr in one year — capital allocation discipline untested at this scale
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on PNGJL yields a clear verdict: it fails the cheapness test entirely. EBIT for FY25 is ₹337 Cr (operating income). Enterprise Value = Market Cap ₹9,061 Cr + Net Debt ₹836 Cr (debt ₹930 Cr - cash ₹94 Cr) ≈ ₹9,897 Cr. That gives an earnings yield of just 3.4% — you need 12%+ to even rank in the Magic Formula universe, and 15%+ to be attractive. At P/E 23.6x with a 6.94% operating margin, the market is pricing in years of flawless execution. The return on capital side is more respectable — ROCE of 19.4% is workable — but not exceptional enough (Greenblatt wants 25%+) to justify the valuation premium. Magic Formula requires BOTH legs to be strong simultaneously.

The structural issue is the business model itself: jewelry retail requires massive gold inventory, funded by borrowings (gold loans). Every rupee of revenue growth consumes working capital, which is why OCF was -₹675 Cr and FCF -₹1,109 Cr in FY25 despite ₹218 Cr of reported net profit. This is the opposite of what Greenblatt loves — a capital-light compounder that earns high returns on incremental invested capital. PNGJL is actually capital-intensive at the margin, with each new store requiring significant inventory financing. The 192-year-old brand (founded 1832) and strong Maharashtra presence provide some moat, but not enough to change the quantitative verdict at current valuations.
